assignments.brief_reason: Explicitly favors free speech while allowing removal only for harm/negative influence.
Describes difficulty making a joint paired decision, without stating why under moderation criteria.
Sets a line at name-calling, swearing, or inciting violence—specific toxicity/threat removal trigger.
Allows most because no direct physical-violence threats are present.
Uses harm-to-a-group as a criterion, consistent with harm-based removal exceptions while generally allowing speech.
General free-speech allowance with an exception when comments feel too degrading.
Focuses on whole-message integration and avoiding group generalization; not clearly free-speech/harm exception or pair-mirror consistency.
Sensationalist language as an influence cue; not clearly framed as harm/toxicity thresholds.
Uses constructiveness tone to guide decisions, but does not map to the threat/toxicity or free-speech exception themes.
Justifies keep/remove based on enabling open discussion rather than the codebook harm/toxicity/free-speech exception axes.
States decisions were driven by gut feelings (process); no fit to the defined moderation themes.
Calls out fairness and avoiding vulgarity; vulgarity aligns with the “remove for threats/toxicity” theme.
Looks for content that sparks debate using both viewpoints; not primarily about paired moderation symmetry or harm/threat exceptions.
Removal/assessment based on how damaging posts are to conversation via derogatory/profane language (toxicity).
Describes marker-based cross-pair comparison steps; not claiming applying same moderation standard across both sides.
Uses vulgarity/ALL CAPS writing-style cues as a keep/remove basis—toxicity-ish content boundary.
Focuses deletions on name calling/invective—explicit toxicity trigger.
Argues for symmetric allowance of misinformation absent measurable harm/incitement; aligns with free speech with violence/threat exceptions.
Fairness without bias is stated as an evaluation principle, but not tied to the specific mirror-pair standardization theme.
Allows viewpoints absent threats/violence and derogatory/racist remarks—conditional removal based on harm/abuse exceptions.
